title: Distance between two points

source.citation: Supplemental randomized practice using the distance relationship F-C01 from the Geometry Website Content Pack, SRC-CART, PDF pages 11–17.

prompt: Find the ordinary distance between A=({{x1}}, {{y1}}) and B=({{x2}}, {{y2}}). All coordinates are in centimeters. Round your answer to two decimal places.

steps.title: Find the coordinate differences
steps.text: Subtract in the same order for both coordinates: B minus A.

steps.title: Apply the distance formula
steps.text: The Pythagorean theorem combines the horizontal and vertical differences.

steps.title: Evaluate and round
steps.text: Keep the square root until the final step, then round the nonnegative distance to two decimal places.

hints: Compute Δx = x₂ − x₁ and Δy = y₂ − y₁. Keep the signs until after squaring.
Square both differences, add the squares, and take the positive square root. Do not subtract the squares.
A distance cannot be negative. Convert your answer to the unit you enter before checking it.
